title: Stamps Scholars Program and Scholarship
program_type: University merit scholarship awarded at admission, selected through a multi-stage invitation-only programme (Honors Program to Presidential Scholars cohort to Stamps Scholars)
funding_type: Full estimated cost of attendance for up to four years plus dedicated enrichment funding (university-funded, cost-shared with the Stamps Scholars Program)
administering_authority: Florida State University - Division of Undergraduate Studies, Presidential Scholars Program, with the FSU Office of Admissions
implementing_agency: Florida State University - Division of Undergraduate Studies, Presidential Scholars Program and Office of Admissions (FSU shares the cost of the award with the Stamps Scholars Program)
programme_action: FSU-Stamps Scholars Program partner-school award, drawn from the Presidential Scholars cohort
description: The Stamps Scholars Program and Scholarship is Florida State University's most prestigious undergraduate merit award, granted annually to five incoming first-year students under FSU's partnership with the Stamps Scholars Program. FSU states that the scholarship provides funding valued up to the full estimated cost of attendance for up to four years, including an out-of-state tuition waiver for non-Florida residents, plus US$20,000 in dedicated enrichment funding. Selection is integrated into the Presidential Scholars Program application: applicants who are admitted to the University Honors Program are considered for the Presidential Scholars Program, advance as semifinalists and finalists, and five of the selected Presidential Scholars are then named Stamps Scholars.

award_types: Funding valued up to the full estimated cost of attendance for up to four years (tuition, fees, housing, food, books/course materials/supplies/equipment, transportation and personal expenses)
Out-of-state tuition waiver for non-Florida residents (FSU states a full out-of-state tuition waiver valued at US$73,080 over four years on its current-students renewal page)
US$20,000 in dedicated enrichment funding (internships, international learning experiences, research, creative and service-learning projects, public service, entrepreneurial development)

Participation in the Presidential Scholars Program: four-year sequence of coursework, first-year residential community, engaged-learning opportunities, and access to the national Stamps Scholars community
programme_structure.award_types_detail: FSU describes the Stamps Scholars Program as the most generous scholarship in university history and a full cost-of-attendance award rather than a fixed-dollar stipend. Stamps Scholars are a subset of the Presidential Scholars cohort (65 incoming students for 2027-2028) and therefore also participate in the Presidential Scholars Program, whose own listed components are a US$14,000 Presidential Scholarship, a US$16,000 Admissions (Vires) Scholarship and US$12,000 of enrichment funding, plus an out-of-state tuition waiver.
programme_structure.renewal_criteria: Automatically renewed each semester if: enrolment in 15 credit hours each semester; a cumulative FSU grade point average of 3.0 or better; and consistent, successful degree progress and course completion. An Admissions Scholarship Modification Request Form exists for limited cases such as credit underloads, summer disbursement, or continuation into FSU graduate coursework.
programme_structure.automatic_consideration: Applicants who apply to the FSU University Honors Program are automatically considered for this invitation-only scholarship programme. There is no separate Stamps application: the Honors Program supplemental essay serves as the Presidential Scholars and Stamps Scholarship application essay.
programme_structure.intake: Fall entry only, as an incoming first-year (first-time-in-college) student. Applications are open for the 2027-2028 academic year.

status_note: Applications for Fall 2027 entry are open as of the verification date. The FSU first-year application and the University Honors Program supplemental essay for scholarship consideration close at 11:59 p.m. EST on 1 December 2026; semifinalist video responses are due 28 February 2027; the finalist recruitment weekend is 2-3 April 2027. The next cycle after this one is Fall 2028 entry, for which FSU's recurring pattern indicates a 1 December 2027 deadline (not yet published).
verification_type: direct official-source verification of programme, admissions and cost pages on fsu.edu
verification_notes: Confirmed against 14 official fsu.edu fetches: the Presidential Scholars Stamps Scholars Program page, the Presidential Scholars application-process and scholarship-benefits pages, the FSU Office of Admissions first-year scholarships page, its renewal-requirements page and its FAQ, the Office of Admissions deadlines page, the University Honors Program scholars-programs and first-year-applicant pages, the international first-year and English-proficiency pages, the Center for Global Engagement international undergraduate tuition-waiver page, the tuition and cost-estimates pages, and an FSU News (news.fsu.edu) announcement dated 4 August 2026. The separate University of Miami Stamps Scholarship is already in the database, so this record covers the Florida State University scheme only.

application_deadline.typical_application_window: Opens 1 August 2026; closes 1 December 2026 for Fall 2027 entry
application_deadline.application_period: 2026-27 admissions cycle for Fall 2027 entry (2027-2028 academic year)
application_deadline.official_rule: FSU: 'To be considered for the Presidential Scholars Program, first-year applicants must first submit an application to Florida State University by Dec. 1, 2026, and select "Yes" to the question "Are you interested in applying to the Honors Program?"' and 'Students must indicate their interest in and complete their supplemental University Honors Program application essay by 11:59 p.m. EST on Dec. 1, 2026, to be considered for the University Honors Program and the Presidential Scholars Program.'
application_deadline.deadline_warning: FSU warns that scholarship funds are limited and students are encouraged to apply early for admission; earlier Early Decision and Early Action deadlines of 15 October 2026 also exist for domestic (Early Action is Florida-residents only) applicants. Supporting materials are due 8 December 2026 and the last acceptable test date is 1 January 2027 for Regular Decision.

programme_duration.official_range: Up to four years (eight semesters) of support
programme_duration.renewal_note: Automatically renewed each semester on meeting the renewal conditions (15 credit hours, cumulative FSU GPA of 3.0 or better, consistent successful degree progress). Students who finish their undergraduate degree in under four years and do not pursue FSU graduate coursework are no longer eligible for the remaining disbursements.

funding.scholarship_type: Full estimated cost-of-attendance merit scholarship plus enrichment funding
funding.monthly_amount_note: FSU publishes no monthly stipend. The award is expressed as funding valued up to the full estimated cost of attendance for up to four years, plus US$20,000 in enrichment funding.
funding.travel_amount_note: No separate travel allowance is published. The US$20,000 enrichment funding may support international learning experiences, and FSU's cost-of-attendance budget includes transportation, but no dedicated travel amount is stated.
funding.fully_funded_note: FSU states the funding is valued up to the full estimated cost of attendance for up to four years, including an out-of-state tuition waiver for non-Florida residents. Coverage is capped at FSU's published estimated cost of attendance, and the out-of-state tuition-waiver component does not apply to study-abroad programmes under FSU's waiver rules.
funding.living_allowance_note: Housing, food, transportation and personal expenses are inside FSU's published estimated cost of attendance (out-of-state, on-campus totals US$43,916 for 2026-2027), rather than being a separately published allowance.
funding.visa_support_note: No visa or immigration-fee support is published. International applicants must complete FSU's Certification of Financial Responsibility form before a Form I-20 can be issued; this is a general F-1 requirement, not a scholarship benefit.
funding.installation_support_note: Not published in the official source.
funding.insurance_note: Health insurance is not addressed in the official sources for this award.

tuition.conditions: Full estimated cost of attendance is covered for up to four years. Non-Florida residents receive a full out-of-state tuition waiver; FSU states the out-of-state tuition waiver for Stamps Scholars is valued at US$73,080 over four years. FSU's 2026-2027 out-of-state undergraduate tuition is US$22,232 per year versus US$5,604 in-state.

monthly_stipend.note: Not published in official source. FSU expresses the award as full estimated cost of attendance, not a stipend.

travel_allowance.note: No separate travel allowance is published.

visa_support.note: Not published in official source. International applicants complete FSU's Certification of Financial Responsibility for the Form I-20, which is a general F-1 requirement.

research_allowance.conditions: Covered through the US$20,000 enrichment funding, which FSU says supports research, creative and service-learning projects as well as internships and public service. Presidential Scholars also participate in the Undergraduate Research Opportunity Program in their first year.

book_allowance.conditions: Books, course materials, supplies and equipment are a component of FSU's published estimated cost of attendance (US$1,380 per year for undergraduates in 2026-2027); no separate book allowance is published.

accommodation_support.conditions: Housing is a component of FSU's published estimated cost of attendance (US$8,420 per year on-campus for undergraduates in 2026-2027). Stamps Scholars also take part in the Presidential Scholars first-year residential community (Landis Hall).

enrichment_funding.conditions: US$20,000 in dedicated enrichment funding across the award to support internships, international learning experiences, research, creative and service-learning projects, public service and entrepreneurial development.

bond.note: No service bond, repayment obligation or residence/work requirement is published. Renewal is conditioned only on enrolment, GPA and degree-progress requirements.

total_estimated_value.note: FSU does not publish a single total dollar value for the Stamps award. Published components are the full estimated cost of attendance for up to four years, an out-of-state tuition waiver stated as valued at US$73,080 over four years, and US$20,000 in enrichment funding. A computed total is deliberately not recorded as an award value.

coverage: Funding valued up to the full estimated cost of attendance for up to four years, including tuition, fees, housing, food, books/course materials/supplies/equipment, transportation and personal expenses
Full out-of-state tuition waiver for non-Florida residents (stated by FSU as valued at US$73,080 over four years)
US$20,000 in dedicated enrichment funding for internships, international learning experiences, research, creative and service-learning projects, public service and entrepreneurial development
Participation in the Presidential Scholars Program: four-year course sequence, first-year residential community, engaged-learning opportunities and the national Stamps Scholars community
Renewable automatically each semester on meeting the renewal conditions
coverage_limitations: FSU's wording is 'funding valued up to the full estimated cost of attendance', so the award is capped at FSU's published estimated cost of attendance rather than being an open-ended benefit; the benefit structure for future cohorts may differ.
Only five awards are made per year and the programme is invitation-only, selected from the Presidential Scholars cohort.
The out-of-state tuition waiver applies only to non-Florida residents; FSU rules out-of-state tuition waivers toward tuition only, not toward study-abroad programmes or other fees.

Whether the Stamps US$20,000 enrichment funding replaces or supplements the US$12,000 Presidential Scholars enrichment allowance is not stated on any official page reviewed; FSU publishes both figures without reconciling them.

FSU publishes two different values for the out-of-state tuition waiver on different official pages (US$73,080 on the current-students renewal page and US$73,808 on the first-year scholarships page, with US$63,555 quoted for Presidential Scholars on the programme's own benefits page), so the exact waiver value should be re-checked before the cycle closes.
FSU has published notice of proposed Market Rate tuition and fee increases effective Fall 2027, so cost-of-attendance and waiver values may change.
The 2026-2027 cost estimates used here are the most recent published; Fall 2027-Spring 2028 budgets for the incoming cohort were not yet published.
Scholarship funds are not available until shortly before the semester begins, so the admissions tuition deposit and orientation registration fees are not covered.
Awards cannot be deferred: a student who cannot attend in the admitted term must reapply and be re-evaluated.
eligible_applicants: Incoming first-year (first-time-in-college) students admitted to Florida State University for Fall entry
High school seniors who apply to the FSU University Honors Program and are admitted to it
Students enrolling in all disciplines and majors; no field restriction is published
Non-Florida residents, who receive the out-of-state tuition waiver component
International applicants, who FSU states use the same application as domestic students and are reviewed under the same holistic admission review process
final_year_condition: The relevant entry requirement is secondary-school completion rather than an existing bachelor's degree: students in the final year of secondary school (high school seniors) are the target applicants, applying as first-time-in-college first-year students for the following Fall.
equivalent_degree_note: FSU reviews applicants with an international educational background using the same holistic admission review as applicants from U.S. high schools. Non-U.S. secondary records require official transcripts plus a Secondary School Evaluation by an independent foreign credential evaluation agency (a NACES member is recommended) showing degree equivalency and a U.S.-equivalent GPA. The evaluation may be waived for applicants whose credentials use a U.S. or IB grading scale or whose programme is a listed examination-based curriculum.
previous_award_restriction: No restriction on holding other scholarships is published. FSU states it typically does not match scholarships from other institutions, and the Presidential/Benacquisto and out-of-state National Merit awards are mutually exclusive alternative packages.

eligibility.citizenship: No citizenship restriction is published for this award. FSU states international first-year applicants use the same application as domestic students and are reviewed using the same holistic admission review process; the award also provides an out-of-state tuition waiver for non-Florida residents, which presupposes non-Florida (including international) recipients. No official fsu.edu page explicitly states that non-U.S. citizens are eligible for the Stamps award, so this is an inference from the absence of a restriction.
eligibility.residence_requirement: No Florida residency requirement; the out-of-state tuition waiver component applies specifically to non-Florida residents.
eligibility.academic_requirements: Holistic review of grades and strength of curriculum, honours and awards, extracurricular achievements, unique individual talents, quality of the Honors prompt response and test scores. FSU states that the minimum criteria vary each year with the applicant pool and that scholarship recipients have typically earned no grades below B. An ACT, CLT or SAT score is required by Florida Board of Governors regulation 6.002.
eligibility.language_requirement: Official English language proficiency results are required of all international applicants whose native language is not English: TOEFL iBT 80 (test taken before 21 January 2026) or 4.0 (on or after 21 January 2026), IELTS Academic 6.5, PTE 55, Michigan Language Assessment 55, Duolingo 125, Cambridge C1 Advanced or C2 Proficiency 180. Scores must be sent directly by the testing agency and are no longer valid after two years.
eligibility.extracurricular_requirement: Extracurricular achievements form part of FSU's holistic review, and the Stamps profile explicitly requires a sustained commitment to service and initiative in leadership.
eligibility.leadership_requirement: Yes. Presidential Scholars nominated for the Stamps Scholarship are selected 'based on the program's established selection criteria and their demonstrated potential for leadership and impact'. FSU states the programme seeks students who embody five pillars: wisdom, leadership, service, character and vision.
eligibility.enrolment_status_requirement: Must be an incoming first-year student entering in the Fall term; the programme is not open to transfer applicants, and scholarship deferral is not permitted.
eligibility.field_restrictions: None. FSU states admission to the programme is open to high school seniors enrolling in all disciplines.

academic_requirements.percentage_note: FSU publishes no fixed percentage, GPA cut-off or test-score threshold for this award. It states that applicants are evaluated holistically and that minimum criteria vary each year depending on the academic profile of the applicant pool.
programme_specific_requirements: Submit the FSU first-year application (institutional application or Common App) by 1 December 2026 and answer 'Yes' to the question 'Are you interested in applying to the Honors Program?'

Complete the supplemental University Honors Program application essay by 11:59 p.m. EST on 1 December 2026 (the same prompt serves the Presidential Scholars and Stamps Scholarship essays; only one response is needed per student)
Submit at least one ACT, CLT or SAT score before the materials deadline (test scores are also required by FL Board of Governors regulation 6.002)
Semifinalists: submit video responses to two prompts by 11:59 p.m. EST on 28 February 2027
Finalists: attend the required on-campus interview during Recruitment Weekend, 2-3 April 2027, in Tallahassee
selection_factors_may_include: Quality of the Honors prompt response
Demonstrated potential for leadership and impact
The five pillars FSU lists for the programme: wisdom, leadership, service, character and vision
Drive, humility and creativity, and the capacity to elevate people around them
academic_requirements.holistic_selection_note: FSU describes a holistic review that includes grades and curriculum strength, honours and awards, extracurricular achievements, unique individual talents, essay quality and test scores, and states that the minimum criteria vary each year with the applicant pool.

english_requirement.test_score_note: English proficiency results are required of international applicants whose native language is not English and apply to undergraduate admission, not specifically to the Stamps award. FSU also lists TOEFL iBT 4.0 for tests taken on or after 21 January 2026 and Cambridge C1 Advanced/C2 Proficiency 180. Scores are official only when sent directly to the Office of Admissions by the testing agency and are no longer valid after two years.

language_of_instruction.language_note: All instruction at FSU's Tallahassee main campus is in English. No other language of instruction is offered for this award.

application_method.application_route: One combined application: submit the FSU first-year application (institutional application at admissions.fsu.edu/undergradapp/first-year or the Common App), answer 'Yes' to the Honors Program question, then complete the University Honors Program supplemental essay in the FSU Admissions Portal once it becomes available (up to 48 hours after the admissions application is submitted).
application_steps: 1. Apply to Florida State University by 1 December 2026 using the institutional application or the Common App, and select 'Yes' to 'Are you interested in applying to the Honors Program?'
2. Wait for the University Honors Program supplemental application to appear on the Application Status Check (up to 48 hours, longer for Common App applicants)

3. Complete the supplemental University Honors Program application essay by 11:59 p.m. EST on 1 December 2026; the same response is used for the Presidential Scholars and Stamps Scholarship applications

4. For international applicants: complete the International School Form, submit official academic records (and a Secondary School Evaluation where required), self-report ACT/CLT/SAT scores, self-report English proficiency results, and submit an essay and resume/list of activities in the Admissions Portal
5. Notification on 18 February 2027 of admission to FSU and University Honors, and of semifinalist selection for the Presidential Scholars Program
6. Semifinalists submit video responses to two prompts by 11:59 p.m. EST on 28 February 2027
7. Finalists attend the required on-campus interview during Recruitment Weekend, 2-3 April 2027, in Tallahassee

8. Presidential Scholars are notified by email shortly after Recruitment Weekend and sign a participation agreement; those nominated for the Stamps Scholarship interview with a member of the Stamps Scholars Program national leadership team
9. Five of the Presidential Scholars cohort are named Stamps Scholars
application_method.application_fee: US$30 first-year application fee, which may be waived for applicants who qualify for an ACT, College Board or NACAC application fee waiver or who meet other indicators of economic need. The scholarship does not waive this fee.

universal_documents: FSU first-year application (institutional application or Common App) with the Honors Program interest question answered 'Yes'
University Honors Program supplemental application essay (250-350 words) - this single essay also serves as the Presidential Scholars and Stamps Scholarship application essay
At least one self-reported ACT, CLT or SAT score
commonly_requested_documents: Semifinalist video responses to two prompts
Participation agreement for Presidential Scholars (signed to be officially enrolled in the programme)

official_application_documents.document_language: Documents must be issued in English or accompanied by certified English translations. Translated records must be literal, not interpretive, and must be signed and dated by an educational official familiar with academic records; notarized translations by officials without educational affiliation are not accepted.
official_application_documents.document_format: Official academic records must be sent directly to FSU by the school, exam board or a school official (a school official may email them to admissions@fsu.edu), or mailed in a sealed envelope directly to FSU. The Secondary School Evaluation must be sent directly from the evaluation agency to Florida State University. Test scores must be sent directly by the testing agency to be considered official.
official_application_documents.transcript_requirement: Official academic records are required, at minimum official school transcripts, and may also include international examination results and/or a secondary school evaluation. A Secondary School Evaluation by an independent foreign credential evaluation agency (a NACES member is recommended) showing degree equivalency and a U.S.-equivalent GPA is required for applicants who attended a secondary school outside the United States or studied a curriculum that did not follow the standard U.S. system.
official_application_documents.letter_of_recommendation_note: No recommendation letters are published as required for this award or for FSU first-year admission.

identity_documents.notes: FSU's published first-year document list does not include a separate identity document for the scholarship; passport details are collected for international applicants through the Admissions Portal and the Certification of Financial Responsibility process.

selection_process.decision_maker: Florida State University Presidential Scholars Program (Division of Undergraduate Studies) and the FSU Office of Admissions, with a final interview conducted by a member of the Stamps Scholars Program's national leadership team
selection_process.selection_type: Multi-stage, invitation-only, merit-based, university-administered; no separate national scholarship application
possible_stages: Stage 1 - Submit the FSU first-year application with Honors interest and complete the University Honors Program supplemental essay by 11:59 p.m. EST on 1 December 2026
Stage 2 - Admission to FSU and to University Honors, plus notification of semifinalist status for the Presidential Scholars Program, on 18 February 2027
Stage 3 - Semifinalists submit video responses to two prompts by 11:59 p.m. EST on 28 February 2027
Stage 4 - Finalists attend a required on-campus interview during Recruitment Weekend, 2-3 April 2027, in Tallahassee
Stage 5 - Presidential Scholars are notified by email shortly after Recruitment Weekend and sign a participation agreement
Stage 6 - Presidential Scholars nominated for the Stamps Scholarship interview with a member of the Stamps Scholars Program's national leadership team as the final step
Stage 7 - Five of the Presidential Scholars cohort are named Stamps Scholars
selection_process.weighting_note: FSU publishes no numeric weighting or scoring formula for this award. It states only that nominees are chosen based on the programme's established selection criteria and their demonstrated potential for leadership and impact, and that the minimum criteria vary each year with the applicant pool.
selection_process.results_timing: 18 February 2027: admission decisions for FSU and University Honors, and semifinalist notification. Late February 2027: semifinalist video responses due 28 February 2027. Early March 2027: finalist notification and invitation. 2-3 April 2027: Recruitment Weekend interviews. Shortly after Recruitment Weekend: Presidential Scholars notification. After the national leadership interview: Stamps Scholars selection.
selection_process.scholarship_rank_note: The Stamps scholarship sits above the Presidential Scholars Program: Stamps Scholars are chosen from among the selected Presidential Scholars cohort (65 incoming students for 2027-2028, increased from 60), and five of them are named Stamps Scholars. All Presidential Scholars are automatically accepted into the University Honors Program.

selection_criteria.additional_factors: FSU lists five pillars the programme seeks: wisdom (exceptional intellectual curiosity), leadership (acting with intention to create meaningful impact), service (sustained commitment for a greater good), character (integrity, resilience and moral courage) and vision (innovate, integrate and motivate). The programme also describes a profile of drive, humility and creativity with a natural capacity to elevate those around them, and expects scholars to act as ambassadors for the institution on national and global stages. Established Stamps selection criteria and demonstrated potential for leadership and impact are the deciding factors at the final stage.

degree_outcome.awarded_qualification: Bachelor's degree from Florida State University; the scholarship itself confers no separate qualification
degree_outcome.typical_programme_length: Four years (eight semesters), which matches the full period of award support
possible_awards: Bachelor's degree (baccalaureate) in any FSU major, at the Tallahassee main campus
degree_outcome.degree_note: The award funds a four-year undergraduate programme at FSU's main campus and is not transferable to other institutions; FSU states its admissions scholarships can only be applied to academic pursuits at FSU. Remaining disbursements may be requested for FSU graduate-level coursework if the undergraduate degree is completed early.
degree_outcome.credit_transfer: No credit transfer is described for the award itself. FSU separately grants accelerated credit for qualifying IB, A-Level, AP and similar credentials as part of first-year admissions.

student_rights_and_cost_protection.tuition_fee_for_recipients: Funding is valued up to the full estimated cost of attendance for up to four years, including a full out-of-state tuition waiver for non-Florida residents. For 2026-2027 FSU's published out-of-state undergraduate estimated cost of attendance is US$43,916 on campus per year against US$26,018 for in-state students.
student_rights_and_cost_protection.application_fee_for_recipients: The US$30 first-year application fee is not waived by the scholarship. FSU states scholarship funds are not available until right before the semester begins, so the admissions tuition deposit and orientation registration fees must be paid separately.
student_rights_and_cost_protection.student_agreement: Presidential Scholars are provided a participation agreement which they should sign to be officially enrolled in the programme. Renewal depends on meeting the published renewal requirements.
student_rights_and_cost_protection.common_services: Presidential Scholars four-year curriculum with Friday afternoon meetings in the first year and monthly Sunday meetings thereafter; first-year residential community in Landis Hall; participation in the Undergraduate Research Opportunity Program in the first year; annual public service experiences; executive, diversity/equity/inclusion and service boards; mentoring from older scholars and alumni; collaboration with the Office of National Fellowships; access to the national community of Stamps Scholars and alumni. Enrichment funding may be used for International Programs, Global Scholars, research and creative projects, service learning, public service, internships and entrepreneurial development.
student_rights_and_cost_protection.bond_requirement: No bond, service obligation or repayment requirement is published for this award.
student_rights_and_cost_protection.bond_breach_consequence: None published. Loss of the award results only from failing the renewal conditions: enrolment below 15 credit hours per semester, a cumulative FSU GPA below 3.0, or inconsistent degree progress and course completion.

application_readiness_checklist: Decide by 1 December 2026 and start early: FSU warns scholarship funds are limited and encourages early admission applications
Draft the Honors supplemental essay around two FSU majors from different departments and an Honors Signature Course at their intersection (250-350 words)
Confirm at least one ACT, CLT or SAT score is reported (test scores must be self-reported on the Admissions Portal, not through the Common App)
Answer 'Yes' to the Honors Program question, then check the Admissions Portal for the Honors application within 48 hours
International applicants: start the International School Form, official transcripts and credential evaluation early, and check whether the Secondary School Evaluation is waived for your curriculum
International applicants: book TOEFL iBT, IELTS Academic, PTE, MLA, Duolingo or Cambridge early enough for scores to be sent directly and remain within the two-year validity window
Be ready to record two video responses by 28 February 2027 if selected as a semifinalist
Be prepared to travel to Tallahassee for Recruitment Weekend, 2-3 April 2027, if selected as a finalist
Prepare for the final interview with a member of the Stamps Scholars Program national leadership team
Plan for the US$30 application fee (or a qualifying fee waiver), the admissions tuition deposit and orientation fees, which the scholarship does not cover until the semester begins
programme_comparison_fields: Award value basis: full estimated cost of attendance (cap = FSU's published cost of attendance) rather than a flat dollar amount
Enrichment funding: US$20,000 dedicated to experiential learning
Out-of-state tuition waiver: full waiver for non-Florida residents
Number of awards: five per year
Enrichment flexibility versus Presidential Scholars' US$12,000 enrichment allowance
Access to the national Stamps Scholars network (4,000+ scholars and alumni)
Renewal conditions: 15 credit hours per semester and a cumulative FSU GPA of 3.0
practical_application_data.motivation_letter_strategy: There is no separate motivation letter; the single Honors supplemental essay doubles as the scholarship essay. Use the prompt (choose two FSU majors from different departments, name and describe an Honors Signature Course at their intersection, state what students should gain, and suggest a campus resource, faculty member or organisation) to demonstrate the five pillars FSU says it seeks: wisdom, leadership, service, character and vision. Evidencing a sustained commitment to service and the capacity to elevate others matters more than listing achievements, because the programme openly describes drive, humility and creativity as the profile it looks for.
profile_fit_labels: High-achieving high school senior seeking a full-ride at a U.S. public flagship
Student with a sustained record of service and community impact
Student interested in undergraduate research, internships or international learning
Applicant targeting the Rhodes, Marshall, Schwarzman, Fulbright, Goldwater or NSF GRFP pathways
Out-of-state or international applicant who needs the out-of-state tuition waiver
Applicant who can travel to Tallahassee for an in-person interview weekend
common_mistakes: Assuming the Stamps award is a separate application with its own deadline - there is none; the Honors essay is the application
Waiting until the Regular Decision 1 December deadline and then being too late for scholarship funds, which FSU warns are limited
Not answering 'Yes' to the Honors Program question on the application, which removes consideration entirely
Self-reporting test scores through the Common App, which FSU does not accept
Assuming no standardized test is needed: Florida Board of Governors regulation 6.002 requires an ACT, CLT or SAT score
Assuming international applicants have a different or later process - they use the same application and the same 1 December deadline
Assuming the award pays the admission deposit and orientation fees - it does not
Assuming aid transfers elsewhere - FSU scholarships can only be applied at FSU, and deferral is not permitted

risk_flags.risk: Extreme selectivity: only five awards per year, drawn from the 65-person Presidential Scholars cohort.
risk_flags.impact: Probability of success for any single applicant is very low, and the practical value of the record depends on treating it as an aspiration plus the broader Presidential Scholars opportunity.
risk_flags.mitigation: Apply to the University Honors Program so that consideration for the Presidential Scholars Program (65 awards) is automatic, and treat the Stamps award as the top tier of a funnel rather than the only outcome.

risk_flags.risk: Final selection requires a required in-person interview and recruitment weekend in Tallahassee on 2-3 April 2027, plus an interview with a member of the Stamps Scholars Program's national leadership team.
risk_flags.impact: Travel cost, visa or scheduling barriers may prevent otherwise strong candidates from completing selection.
risk_flags.mitigation: Confirm travel feasibility before committing to the finalist stage; plan the itinerary early and budget separately for the trip, which the scholarship does not cover before disbursement.

risk_flags.risk: Official fsu.edu pages publish conflicting out-of-state tuition-waiver values (US$73,080 versus US$73,808, and US$63,555 for Presidential Scholars on the programme's own benefits page).
risk_flags.impact: The dollar value of the non-tuition portion of the package cannot be stated precisely.
risk_flags.mitigation: Record the full cost-of-attendance basis rather than a computed total, and confirm the waiver value with presidentialscholars@fsu.edu before relying on it.

risk_flags.risk: FSU has published notice of proposed Market Rate tuition and fee increases effective Fall 2027, and the Fall 2027-Spring 2028 cost-of-attendance estimates were not yet published at verification time.
risk_flags.impact: Cost estimates and waiver values for the incoming cohort may change.
risk_flags.mitigation: Re-check tuition.fsu.edu cost estimates and the proposed fee-increase page before the application deadline and again in spring 2027.

risk_flags.risk: International (non-U.S. citizen) eligibility is inferred rather than explicitly stated on the official pages.
risk_flags.impact: An international applicant could invest significant effort on an assumption that is not directly confirmed.
risk_flags.mitigation: Email presidentialscholars@fsu.edu to confirm international eligibility and how the out-of-state waiver is applied to international students before applying.

risk_flags.risk: The application essay, transcript, credential evaluation and English-test requirements are all due under tight dates (1 December 2026 application and essay, 8 December 2026 materials, 28 February 2027 videos).
risk_flags.impact: A missing credential evaluation or late test score can remove an applicant from consideration even with strong grades.
risk_flags.mitigation: For international applicants, start the International School Form, official records, credential evaluation and English test months in advance and track the personalised checklist in the Admissions Portal.

risk_flags.risk: Award deferral is not permitted and funds cannot be transferred to another institution.
risk_flags.impact: A change of plans in the admitted term forfeits the award and requires reapplying.
risk_flags.mitigation: Confirm that Fall 2027 entry at FSU's Tallahassee campus is certain before accepting, since a student who cannot attend must reapply and be re-evaluated.

risk_flags.risk: FSU's out-of-state tuition waiver rules exclude study-abroad programmes and cover tuition only, not other fees.
risk_flags.impact: The waiver portion cannot be used for study abroad, so some enrichment-based international experiences must be funded from the US$20,000 enrichment allowance or other sources.
risk_flags.mitigation: Plan international learning within the enrichment funding and note that admissions scholarships other than the waiver can be used toward FSU International Programs.

application_status_workflow: FSU first-year application submitted with Honors interest indicated
University Honors supplemental essay submitted (by 11:59 p.m. EST, 1 December 2026)
Admitted to FSU and University Honors / selected as Presidential Scholars semifinalist (18 February 2027)
Finalist invited to Recruitment Weekend interviews (early March 2027)
Invited into the Presidential Scholars Program and participation agreement signed
Nominated for the Stamps Scholarship and interviewed by the Stamps Scholars Program national leadership team
Named a Stamps Scholar (five per year)
Enrolled with award disbursed each semester on meeting renewal conditions
best_fit: A high-achieving high school senior with a strong, sustained record of service and leadership who wants a full cost-of-attendance award at a U.S. public flagship, can submit the Honors supplemental essay by 1 December 2026, and can travel to Tallahassee for an in-person interview weekend in April 2027. It is especially attractive to out-of-state and international applicants because the package includes a full out-of-state tuition waiver, and to students who intend to use enrichment funding for undergraduate research, internships or international learning.
not_best_fit: Transfer applicants or students who have already begun college - the award is for incoming first-year entry only
Applicants who need need-based aid; selection is merit-based and no financial-need assessment is part of it
Applicants who cannot travel to Tallahassee for the required in-person interview weekend
Applicants who cannot meet the 1 December 2026 essay deadline or who do not want to take an ACT, CLT or SAT
Applicants seeking a graduate or master's-level award, or a scholarship at an institution other than FSU
Applicants expecting a published fixed dollar total value or a monthly stipend
Applicants who want the award to cover the admissions deposit, orientation fees or a study-abroad programme's out-of-state charges

image.logo_verification_method: The official fsu.edu pages under presidentialscholars.fsu.edu, admissions.fsu.edu and honors.fsu.edu all render the same FSU institutional mark from www.fsu.edu. An HTTP request to that asset URL returned 200 with Content-Type image/svg+xml on 2026-10-03, confirming the file is live on FSU's own domain. The Stamps Scholars Program's own logo is referenced by the page only from a Pantheon sandbox host (live-fsu-undergradsandbox.pantheonsite.io), which is not an official fsu.edu domain, so that mark was not used.
image.image_usage_note: The only photographs used on the official Stamps Scholars Program page are served from a non-production sandbox host (live-fsu-undergradsandbox.pantheonsite.io) rather than from fsu.edu, and FSU News photographs are credited to staff photographers. No verified official fsu.edu photograph asset was therefore recorded for this award.

Letters of recommendation are not published as a requirement anywhere in the FSU first-year admissions or Honors/Presidential Scholars process for this award.

Approximation note: 'full cost of attendance' is FSU's capped estimated cost of attendance, not an unlimited benefit; FSU's own published out-of-state on-campus undergraduate estimate for 2026-2027 is US$43,916 per year.
The Honors supplemental essay prompt quoted in document_checklist is the 2026 cycle prompt published by the University Honors Program; the prompt may change for later cycles.
